clue.text: Resources left to add the final touch

parts.note: capital means financial resources or funds

explanation.surface: Funds bequeathed to someone so they can put the finishing flourish on a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resources left' reads like an inheritance, but it splits into CAPITAL and L, which together are read as a three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown something, giving it a final topping, is the idiom meaning to complete or round off.

clue.text: What the carpenter cuts out in one piece

definitions.meaning: read as three words, an opening made with a saw by a joiner

explanation.definitionFit: Altogether, the phrase meaning the entirety; split differently it is an opening cut by a woodworker's saw.

clue.text: Hindu who reckons it'll be a fine autumn

parts.note: a Hindu is typically an Indian
one who reckons or adds up figures is a summer

explanation.surface: A man in India forecasting a mild end to the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who reckons' gives SUMMER, one who sums; the word has nothing to do with the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means a spell of warm, dry weather late in the year after summer.

clue.text: Brave despite a soft, dull pain

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
an ache is a dull persistent pain

explanation.surface: Someone courageously carrying on in spite of a mild nagging hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a Native American warrior, of whom an Apache is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Apache are a Native American people.

clue.text: Look to an accommodating banker for it

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Hoping a helpful bank manager will lend you the money.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: an obliging bank manager provides money for this.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum advanced by a bank to a borrower is credit provided as accommodation.

clue.text: Timetable for education in a German school

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Schule is the German word for school

explanation.surface: The class timetable for learning at a school in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The German word for school is borrowed whole, and 'in' signals that the abbreviation for education sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan of times for events, a programme or timetable.

clue.text: I get smuggled out of Middle Eastern country

parts.note: to run goods, as in gun-running, is to smuggle them, so ran

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking illegally out of a nation in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggled' gives RAN, as in running guns or contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: The Islamic Republic in the Gulf region, formerly Persia.

clue.text: Heroic act in action is foiled

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a feat is a heroic or remarkable act

explanation.surface: A brave exploit in the field has been thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Thwarted, beaten or overcome; plans that are foiled have been beaten.

clue.text: Foreign Office reverts to regimen, as expected

indicators.note: reverts tells us the abbreviation for the ministry is turned back to front

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry
a regimen, like a course of treatment, is a course

explanation.surface: A government department going back to its old routine, which surprised nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverts' turns FO into OF; then a course of treatment supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally, certainly: the stock phrase said when something happens just as anticipated.

clue.text: Exclude copper from group

parts.note: to ban is to exclude or bar
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: Someone throwing a policeman out of their circle of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman or the metal Cu; here it is a penny, abbreviated d in pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a company of people joined together, synonym for a group or troupe.

clue.text: In conclusion study debating

indicators.note: In at the start tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an inference is a conclusion drawn from evidence
to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Ending a period of study with a spell of discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the stock phrase 'In conclusion', but it is the container signal; 'study' is the old verb con, to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a meeting for discussion means taking part in formal talks, i.e. debating.

clue.text: Charming habit when starting to drive

parts.note: engaging means charming or attractive
a habit is clothing, as is gear

explanation.surface: Describing an appealing outfit worn when setting off in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a routine; it means clothing, like a nun's habit, giving GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a car into first so it moves is the action of a motorist pulling away.

clue.text: Relaxed orchestra prepared to come in on it

definitions.meaning: laid-back, gloomy-free in a low-key way; an informal or understated manner

definitions.text: orchestra prepared to come in on it
definitions.meaning: the conductor's downward stroke marking the first beat of the bar, when players enter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both understated or low-key, and the conductor's opening down-stroke on which musicians start playing.

clue.text: Spare key is yours

parts.note: spare means lean or thin
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Telling someone the extra key belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare key' reads as a duplicate key; 'Spare' means THIN and 'key' is the musical key E.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic possessive pronoun for you, used as in old-fashioned speech.

clue.text: Ancient Babylonian man is very important

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Sumer and Babylonia
gent, short for gentleman, means a man

explanation.surface: A figure from ancient Mesopotamia being described as a person of great significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient Babylonian' reads as a person, but it is the city of UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing and requiring immediate attention is of great importance.

clue.text: List of courses for fellows going to university

parts.note: fellows are men, chaps

explanation.surface: A prospectus of degree courses for young men heading off to college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' and 'university' suggest academic study, but the courses are dishes at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare lists the dishes, the starters, mains and desserts.

clue.text: Home isn't refurbished for the landlord

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A house that has not been renovated, according to the owner who lets it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an old jocular term for a pub landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned jocular term for the publican or innkeeper.

clue.text: Express an opinion, while deputy admits nothing

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: vice, as in vice-president, means a deputy
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Speaking your mind, while your second-in-command confesses to having nothing to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like a confession; it is the container signal putting O into VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice a view is to state it aloud, verb meaning to articulate a thought.

clue.text: Whims lead to changes when investing silver

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: varies means changes
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Sudden fancies cause swings in policy when putting money into precious metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' looks financial, but it means clothing or surrounding, an old sense of invest.
explanation.definitionFit: Caprices and unpredictable fancies, plural noun for erratic notions.

clue.text: Cheerful young FBI agent

parts.note: a G-man is American slang for an FBI agent, giving G
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A bright and happy rookie at the Bureau.
explanation.walkthrough: An FBI agent is a G-man, so a young one is playfully a G-lad. G-man is US slang for a federal agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad means happy and pleased, a plain synonym for cheerful.

clue.text: Aided son to correct nasal disorder

indicators.note: to correct means to put right, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent helps their boy get a problem with his nose fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lymph tissue at the back of the nose; enlarged ones cause breathing trouble.

clue.text: Margaret joins teaching union for added spice

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain
Meg is a short form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: A woman named Margaret signing up with a teachers' union, adding some zest.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's largest teachers' union, the National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, grated as a flavouring.

clue.text: Jeopardise a call for peace

definitions.meaning: to put at risk or imperil
read as two words, an appeal to stop being furious and make peace

explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to put at risk; split in two, the word is a plea to stop fury.

clue.text: They bore the doctor with complaints

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
ills are complaints or ailments

explanation.surface: Patients finding the GP tedious because of his talk of illnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' seems to mean tire; it means make holes, which is what these tools do.
explanation.definitionFit: Power tools that make holes, noun plural matching the verb phrase 'they bore'.

clue.text: Said her rings need styling by a coiffeuse

indicators.note: need here suggests the letters require rearranging into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman remarking that her curls want setting by a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' signals that SAID HER RINGS must be rearranged; the rings of hair are the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiffeuse is a female hair stylist, so her styling work is cutting and setting hair.

clue.text: A desire to scratch?

parts.note: reads as wanting to scrape something away, but describes the skin irritation itself, and also a restless yearning

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a skin irritation demanding scratching and, figuratively, a restless longing.

clue.text: Bean always very large when pulled up

indicators.note: pulled up in a down clue tells us the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: ay, or aye, is a poetic word for always
OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for very large

explanation.surface: A huge bean plant growing ever upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' reverses AY and OS together, from AYOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The legume grown widely for its protein-rich seeds, used for tofu and milk.

clue.text: End of the Devil and sin

indicators.note: End of the tells us the letters come from the tail of the next word

explanation.surface: Satan's downfall and wrongdoing in general.
explanation.walkthrough: The last four letters of 'Devil' give the answer; the apt surface makes this almost an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness and wrongdoing; a sin is an evil act.

clue.text: Undoubtedly accommodates Maastricht negotiators safely

indicators.note: accommodates means houses or takes in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: surely means undoubtedly, certainly
the EC, European Community, negotiated the Maastricht Treaty of 1992

explanation.surface: Certainly provides a secure home for the diplomats behind a European treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maastricht Treaty was signed by members of the EC, the European Community, giving EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly and without risk, adverb meaning in a way protected from harm.

clue.text: Jack has a way to trick which is hard to understand

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a ruse is a trick or ploy

explanation.surface: A sailor knows a method of deceiving which is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor, AB (able-bodied seaman); 'way' gives ST for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure, recondite and difficult to grasp.
